runs.title: Twenty-third check: the four-week re-check of our grades, and two new ledger rows
runs.summary: 22 Oct: we re-checked the 34 projects we last graded on 28 Sep against their current code: 33 keep their grade (3 of them after a full re-read of changed code), and 1 could not be re-checked because the source is no longer online. 197 entries (2 new); controls ledger 84 studies, 74 with a wiring null: helps 31, no difference 21, worse 6, mixed 13, not yet scored 3; fly wiring beat scrambled wiring in 31 of 74. neural-canvas: loads; brain simulation not seen in our headless browser without a GPU (checked 2026-10-22).

runs.title: Twenty-second check: the 30 spikes/s matched test with a second input draw, and eight new ledger rows
runs.summary: With a second input draw, the matched scrambled brains again sent no turn command (2 input draws on the same 4 scrambled brains). With this input the real brain's turn signal on the right side was 6 spikes/s against our threshold of 5, so the real brain itself sits close to our turn rule at this stimulus strength. Walked in the body, the matched scrambled brain with a small steering signal changed the fly's heading by about 1.3 degrees away from the shadow compared with no brain input, under our 10-degree turn rule; the real brain, with the same input, turned it away by about 9.2 degrees (one run each). With this input the real brain's own turn was also under our 10-degree rule. This body run turns the brain's firing rates into steering through our own hand-made mapping; it is not a separate test of the wiring. 195 entries (9 new); controls ledger 82 studies, 72 with a wiring null: helps 30, no difference 20, worse 6, mixed 13, not yet scored 3; fly wiring beat scrambled wiring in 30 of 72.

runs.title: Twenty-first check: Fly Worker's game panel, the browser demos re-checked, and nine new ledger rows
runs.summary: In our browser checks of 3, 6, 11, 17, 18 and 20 Oct 2026, 9 of 13 demos ran on a machine without a GPU at their latest check. Fly Worker, re-checked 20 Oct: ran by our check's rule, and two screenshots of its game panel taken about 6 seconds apart show the game view, its frame counter and the brain-activity dots changing. Screenshots cannot show whether the brain model drives the game; that is a code question. flyproject.io, first checked 20 Oct: loaded, but showed no activity; about 40 MB transferred, mostly 3D model files. The page kept our slow no-GPU machine busy for most of the check, so a faster machine may differ. 186 entries (15 new); controls ledger 74 studies, 65 with a wiring null: helps 28, no difference 15, worse 6, mixed 13, not yet scored 3; fly wiring beat scrambled wiring in 28 of 65.

runs.title: Twentieth check: the beginner guide re-tested, and a strengthened scrambled brain walked in the body
runs.summary: Re-test, 19 October 2026: 6 of 6 tests, 82.0 Hz bit-exact. Quick look (200 ms trials), run on 19 Oct 2026 in 1.7 min: sugar 80.0 Hz → extend proboscis; shuffled wiring 0.0 Hz → stay still. Shorter trials are noisier than the full run. 19 Oct: walked in the body, the one matched scrambled brain with a small steering signal changed the fly's heading by about 1.4 degrees away from the shadow compared with no brain input, under our 10-degree turn rule; the real brain, with the same input, turned it away by about 16.8 degrees (one run each). This body run turns the brain's firing rates into steering through our own hand-made mapping; it is not a separate test of the wiring. 171 entries (10 new, two of them U rows); controls ledger 65 studies, 56 with a wiring null: helps 25, no difference 12, worse 5, mixed 12, not yet scored 2; activity numbers now say what they count.

runs.title: Nineteenth check: the 30 spikes/s scrambled brains strengthened, and a browser correction
runs.summary: 18 Oct: we then strengthened the connections inside scrambled brains (not the input) until their neurons outside the stimulated input fired about as many spikes as in the real brain (within 30%; same input, one 1-second trial each). On the left side, 2 scrambled brains matched this way, and neither sent a turn command. On the right side, 2 scrambled brains matched this way, and neither sent a turn command. Matching the number of spikes does not match the pattern: 1,152 to 2,228 neurons fired in the matched scrambled brains, against 379 (left) and 432 (right) in the real brain. 1 of the matched scrambled brains sent small steering signals, which we did not walk in the body. As at 80 spikes/s, none of the scrambled brains we ran at 30 spikes/s sent a turn command, including those strengthened to about the real brain's activity outside the input. Correction, 18 Oct: our 17 Oct check loaded fly67's old address, which answered 'not found'; the project now lives at gexhaw.github.io/fly67/. At that address it ran on 18 Oct. Fly Worker, re-checked 18 Oct: ran by our check's rule (two workers and WebAssembly started, and text on the page changed); our screenshots showed only the top of the page, so we did not see the fly itself. Latest no-GPU browser check: 3 of 6 ran (17 Oct; fly67 and Fly Worker re-checked 18 Oct). 3 Oct: 3 of 6. 161 entries (5 new, one a U verdict row on the Odyssey-3 claim); controls ledger 62 studies, 53 with a wiring null: helps 25, no difference 11, worse 4, mixed 11, not yet scored 2; a caveat marker for reading only on 8 ledger rows.

runs.title: Eighteenth check: scrambled brains at 30 spikes/s, and the browser demos re-checked
runs.summary: 17 Oct: at 30 spikes/s, the weakest tested input at which the real brain's turn command appeared, we also ran 2 scrambled brains per side (each neuron keeps its number of connections; one 1-second trial each, with the same trial seed as the real-wiring body runs). On the left side, neither scrambled brain sent a turn command, and their steering signals were identical to having no brain, so in the body they walk like the no-brain fly (the real wiring turned it about 11 deg). On the right side, neither scrambled brain sent a turn command, and their steering signals were identical to having no brain, so in the body they walk like the no-brain fly (the real wiring turned it about 17 deg). As at 80 spikes/s, none of the scrambled brains we ran produced the turn; at 30 spikes/s we did not turn their activity up to match the real brain. The scrambled brains were not matched for overall activity: they fired 48% (left) and 44% (right) as many spikes as the real brain at this strength. Most of those spikes were the stimulated input neurons themselves; outside the input, the scrambled brains fired about 1% as many spikes as the real brain. These body runs turn the brain's firing rates into steering through our own hand-made mapping, so they show the brain result in degrees; they are not a separate test of the wiring. We ran scrambled brains at 30 and 80 spikes/s, not at 20, 40 or 60. Re-checked 17 Oct in the same no-GPU browser: 1 of 6 ran (3 Oct: 3 of 6). 156 entries (4 new); controls ledger 60 studies, 51 with a wiring null: helps 24, no difference 11, worse 4, mixed 10, not yet scored 2. New ledger rows: flycraft-hexapod (in the author's test the real nerve-cord graph moved the hexapod 0.85 mm forward in 8 s, fully rewired graphs 3.5 mm backward, and a time-shuffled real signal 0.72 mm; the author's results file is marked pending the author's own review, and the paper's acceptance is the author's statement only) and fly-connectome-reservoir (its separate reservoir test scores real wiring 100%, target-permuted wiring 83.9% and no connections 50% (3 seeds); a raw-stimulus readout also reaches 100%).

runs.title: Seventeenth check: the right-eye relay reading with 10 matched controls
runs.summary: The relay headline stays: "The two sides disagree: on one side silencing the relays lowered the turn neuron's rate more than matched activity elsewhere, on the other it did not. We do not draw a conclusion." 15 Oct: we ran 5 more matched controls on the right side, 10 in all. Every one of them left the turn neuron's rate higher than silencing the relays did (controls 38-47 Hz, relays 25.7 Hz), so the right-side reading did not change. Our rule compares the relays with the lowest matched control, so extra controls can only make the relays look less special, never more. (5 seeds per side; 5 matched draws on the left and 10 on the right.) 8 new entries (152 in total); controls ledger 58 studies, 49 with a wiring null: helps 22, no difference 11, worse 4, mixed 10, not yet scored 2. fly-pokemon-pi5-stream (the Pokémon-on-a-Raspberry-Pi stream) re-graded from its public code (ianwes92/fly-brain-plays-pokemon) from U to B, borderline C: whole FlyWire FAFB v783 graph as a leaky integrate-and-fire network; game RAM mapped to visual neurons; a hand-written priority arbiter picks the keys; chat keys and a paid override can replace the fly's keys; only Kenyon-cell to MBON learning; no shuffled-wiring control; the stream was not watched.

runs.title: Sixteenth check: the looming turn in degrees, at each input strength
runs.summary: Left eye: In the body, the fly turned away from 30 spikes/s per looming neuron upward on this side, the strength at which the brain's turn command appeared; the turn was about 11 deg at 30 and about 37 deg at 80 (our mapping turns the brain's rates into steering). Right eye: At 30 spikes/s the turn was borderline: the fly turned away in 1 of 2 runs on this side; from 40 upward it turned away in every run. The right-eye borderline rests on one run (seed 0 at 30 spikes/s, 9.18 deg against the 10 deg rule). These body runs turn the brain's firing rates into steering through our own hand-made mapping, so they show the brain result in degrees; they are not a separate test of the wiring. No scrambled brains were run at these strengths. Four descriptive body lines under the 13 Oct relay headline, which stays. 4 new entries (144 in total), none with a wiring control (53 studies, 44 with a wiring null); repositories of 14 of 21 verdict rows re-checked.

runs.title: Fifteenth check: the relays against an activity-matched control, and can a fly brain learn?
runs.summary: The two sides disagree: on one side silencing the relays lowered the turn neuron's rate more than matched activity elsewhere, on the other it did not. We do not draw a conclusion. (relays against an activity-matched control, brain only, pre-registered; 5 seeds and 5 matched draws per side). A fifth plain answer: what changes with practice in 13 projects. 6 new entries (140 in total); 3 new ledger rows (53 studies, 44 with a wiring null, helps 21); ChessFly and fly67 moved by their owner to gexhaw; repositories of 14 of 21 verdict rows re-checked.

runs.title: Fourteenth check: our flyvis motion test ran out of memory again, and 10 entries re-checked in code
runs.summary: Not decided: a second, lower-memory attempt on 12 Oct also needed more memory than our shared machine has (about 3 GB at its peak; the machine allows 3 GB for everything running on it). No result, no ledger row, no chart. 10 graded entries re-checked in code: no grade changed, two texts fixed. One new ledger row (duth-x-stepmania, helps, by the authors' numbers; one seed): 50 studies, 41 with a wiring null, helps 19. 2 new entries (134 in total); 56 videos with refreshed view counts; lead scan: nothing promoted.

runs.title: Thirteenth check: the controls ledger catches up, and 4 new entries
runs.summary: Five studies joined the controls ledger from the authors' own numbers, read by our fixed rules: fly-distill mixed, a mushroom-body odour model worse, brainlab no difference, MelanoGraph helps (weak), fly-arithmetic worse. The ledger has 49 studies, 40 with a wiring null: helps 18, no difference 9, worse 4, mixed 8, not yet scored 1. Three catalogue flags changed; 4 new entries (132 in total); fly-arithmetic's website ran in our browser check; 56 videos with refreshed view counts; lead scan: nothing promoted.

runs.title: Twelfth check: our flyvis motion test did not run, and 3 new entries with their own wiring controls
runs.summary: Our pre-registered test of whether the real wiring layout helps a trained fly vision model (flyvis) see which way things move did not run: "Not decided: the test did not run, because it needed more memory than our shared machine has. A pre-registered setup check also failed, so no result would have been read." One short simulation of the 45,669-cell model was stopped three times for lack of memory (peak about 3.0 of 3 GiB); no result, no ledger row, no chart. 3 new grade A entries with their own real-versus-shuffled comparisons (fly-distill: no difference, a random graph did best; a mushroom-body model on BANC: mixed; brainlab: activity only), the fly-with-me trained-part correction, 128 entries, 44 control studies and 56 videos; lead scan: nothing promoted.

runs.title: Eleventh check: the relay neurons read by firing rate, and what the map leaves out, in numbers
runs.summary: Our pre-registered brain-only relay test, read by firing rate: silencing the relays lowered the turn command to about 60-70% of normal, but silencing random active neurons also moved it, so this is not yet specific to the relays ("Silencing other active neurons also changed the turn command, so this relay result is not specific to the relay neurons."; the left normal range is 1 Hz wide and the random control one draw per eye; one model, not a real fly). A table of what the map leaves out (8 parts, one number and one source each), the flyvis code read, 4 new entries (125), 44 control studies and 56 videos.

runs.title: Tenth check: how strong must the shadow be? A threshold for the turn command, relays silenced, the looming body test at n 6 and one environment for brain and body
runs.summary: Our pre-registered brain-only input series: the turn command appeared from about 30 spikes per second per looming neuron (38% of our strongest input) on both sides, with the escape neuron at the same input (one model; the input is a rate we set, not a measured response to a real shadow). Relays silenced: the turn rule still passed, while the far-side rate fell with PVLP141 silenced. The looming body test at n 6 (6 of 6 real, 0 of 3 scrambled body runs), Brian2 and FlyGym in one Python 3.12 environment (1.1 GB, numpy 2.3.5), a "learns to hack" verdict (U), 121 entries, 43 control studies and a Use in class plan.

runs.title: Ninth check: where in the wiring is the turn? Busy scrambled brains, an "Is it AI?" field, download sizes and five more browser demos
runs.summary: Our pre-registered brain-only looming follow-up: We turned the scrambled maps up until they were as busy as the real one. They still did not produce the turn: the wiring, not the amount of activity, makes it. Inside-only scramble: Scrambling only the inside of the map kept about -9% of the turn command and 69% of the escape signal. Giant fibre silenced: With the escape neuron silenced, the turn command stayed. (expected from the map). Brain only; 7 drives await body runs. Ledger 41 studies (helps 15 of 33; our looming row now fair and strong). trained_class on 116 records (45 of 83 graded with a trained part). Download facts for 8 releases. Five more browser demos, all ran. 5 new entries, 54 videos.

runs.title: Eighth check: we ran the map. A looming shadow, the fly's wiring and a simulated turn, plus four plain answers and 4 new entries
runs.summary: Our own pre-registered looming test: with the real FlyWire map a shadow on one eye turned our simulated FlyGym fly away in 4 of 4 runs, with scrambled maps in 0 of 3 (small n; much quieter scrambled brains; one model, open loop, our hand-made mapping, a constant external walking drive, 1 s; not a real fly). fly67's brain rule reproduced in Brian2 (giant fibre 111.5-120.5 Hz); fly67 stays B. Beginner re-test passed (82.0 Hz bit-exact). Sourced answers to four common questions. 111 entries (4 new), 53 videos with a language field, ledger 38 studies (helps 13 of 30), verdicts 13 current / 7 no code.

runs.title: Seventh check: does it actually run? Six fly-brain browser demos loaded, a flyvis dossier and 3 new entries
runs.summary: Our own headless-browser check of six fly-brain demos (Chromium 154, Linux, no GPU; not a play test): 3 ran (Fly Worker 17.55 MB, FLY67 33.28 MB, flybrain.app 12.72 MB), 2 loaded then froze (most likely software WebGL), 1 stopped at our 1.6 GB memory limit; no demo computed on a server. flyvis dossier: numbers quoted from the full text, ablation wording corrected, 50 pretrained models' validation losses (median 5.300), no shuffled-wiring control. Verdict freshness 13 current, 7 no code. fly-cartpole now helps but does not beat its linear map or LQR. 104 entries and 52 videos re-checked, FlyDoom link gone, 3 new entries (ChessFly A, flypoker C, neurafly C).

runs.title: Sixth check: who does the walking? We gave the fly brain a body, refereed the Terraria fly and added 4 entries
runs.summary: Our own pre-registered body test: the Shiu et al. brain model drove FlyGym's walking fly through our hand-made mapping; the fly walked 13.9 mm in 1 s with the real brain, 14.1 mm with scrambled brains (identical drives) and 14.3 mm with a brainless constant drive; the real brain added turning commands, sugar sent no walking command, and the mapping caps the drive. The reflex test's gain check was not matched on 3 shuffles (MN9 0 Hz at every gain); no scoring rule changed. Terraria fly graded B (no control). 100 entries and 51 videos re-checked (0 grade changes, FlyDoom still gone), 4 new entries and 1 video, fly-cartpole updated to 077dcba, and Add a body tested on Build your own.

runs.title: Fifth check: we scrambled the fly brain four ways, two viral video claims refereed and 6 new entries
runs.summary: Our own pre-registered reflex test on the sugar reflex: real wiring 85.2 Hz; degree-preserving and weight shuffles 0 Hz (5 each, silent); interior-only shuffle 39 Hz (retention 0.46); sign shuffle 214 Hz only because the whole brain ignites; gain check 0 Hz but not matched, so our own ledger row scores mixed, unfair and weak by the fixed rules. Gorilla Tag (527,756 views) and a Roblox fight video graded U. 94 entries and 49 videos re-checked (0 grade changes, FlyDoom repository gone), 6 new entries and 2 videos, a Doom autopilot chart, and Build your own re-tested.

runs.title: Fourth check: does fly wiring help? 31 control studies compared, a FlyLeno verdict and 12 new entries
runs.summary: 82 entries and 47 videos re-checked: 7 repositories with new commits, 3 new releases, 0 grade changes, 0 link failures, 0 videos removed. A new page and data file compare 31 control studies: real fly wiring beat scrambled wiring in 10 of 23, mostly reflex, sensory and steering circuits, and tied or lost in trained, reservoir and ML tasks (7); the fly network beats a no-brain baseline in only 2 of 13. FlyLeno graded B (borderline C). 12 new entries and 2 videos; catalogue records gain controls and wiring_effect fields.

runs.title: Third check: two viral fly-brain claims refereed, DesktopFly re-graded to C and a wiring test where scrambled wiring fails
runs.summary: 73 entries and 44 videos re-checked: 3 new releases, 1 re-grade (DesktopFly B to C), all links responding. Verdicts on two claims with no published code, both grade U: the Raspberry Pi 5 Pokémon stream (input read from game memory, unpublished decoder, chat steers learning) and the Rainbow Six Siege claim (over 1,000,000 neurons matches no fly connectome). 9 new entries and 3 videos, including a grade A study in which scrambled wiring stops a whole-brain fly steering to targets. New DesktopFly project page with a download-lure warning.

runs.title: Second check: 15 new fruit fly brain projects, a Doom control study and two viral claims that do not hold up
runs.summary: 58 entries and 40 videos re-checked about 22 hours after the first pass: no changes, 0 link problems. 15 new entries (5 A, 1 B, 5 C, 2 D, 2 not graded) and 4 new videos. A third-party control study found that a brainless constant autopilot survives in Doom about as long as DOOMFLY's full brain (51.9 s vs 53.3 s); the Half-Life video's connectome claim is contradicted by its code (grade D). New project pages for DOOMFLY and the Shiu et al. model.

runs.title: Video gallery: 40 fruit fly brain videos checked, and an inline-player test
runs.summary: 40 videos matched to the catalogue (35 original uploads, 5 reposts or commentary; 21 of 58 entries now have a video), each with its catalogue grade and what it does not show. YouTube, Vimeo, TikTok and X players all failed inside the site's sandboxed frames, so videos open on their original platform.

runs.title: First catalogue check: fruit fly brain simulation projects, viral claims and a tested beginner project
runs.summary: 58 projects graded from code, verdicts on 12 viral claims, 13 controlled studies, 7 connectome datasets compared, and a beginner simulation run from an empty folder on 2 CPUs (MN9 85.2 Hz with real wiring, 0 Hz with shuffled wiring).
